Barangays are the frontline service delivery points for basic government services to the community. They are responsible for providing financial assistance, distributing relief goods and other resources, announcing community programs, and maintaining contact with residents. However, many barangays continue to rely on manual, paper-based or fragmented processes for these vital services, even in the digital age of technology. These traditional methods often lead to delays, inaccuracies in record keeping, inefficiencies in coordination, and a lack of transparency that affects both the barangay personnel and residents.

One of the common problems of barangays is the management of financial assistance and payout programs. These lists are manually prepared; therefore, the verification process is time consuming and the results are liable to errors like duplicate entries, missing records, wrong information etc. Relief goods, medical supplies, and other assistance are often distributed without a centralized tracking system, making it difficult to inventory supplies, distribution status, and records of recipients. This can lead to inefficient allocation of resources and a lack of accountability.

Another challenge is the distribution of announcements and community events. Many barangays still rely on bulletin boards, printed notices, public address systems or social media platforms that do not effectively reach all residents. This can mean that members of the community will not receive crucial information about meetings, vaccination drives, emergency advisories, when payments will be made and other public services. The lack of a central communication platform further restricts residents’ ability to access timely, reliable information.

The growing need for effective public service has driven local government units to implement digital solutions that enhance operational efficiency and citizen engagement. Information systems on the web have the potential to automate administrative functions, centralize records, increase transparency and speed communications between government offices and the public. Integrating several barangay functions into a single platform allows local officials to reduce manual workloads, increase record accuracy and provide more efficient services.

To tackle these issues, the proposed system MASID: An Integrated Barangay E-Services Web Application: Streamlining Payouts, Resource Distribution, and Events Dissemination in Barangay 442, Sampaloc, Manila provides a complete web-based solution that brings together essential barangay services in a single centralized platform. The app aims to digitize the beneficiary management, automate the payout schedule, and monitoring, facilitate resource inventory and distribution, and provides an effective means for broadcasting announcements, events and public information to the residents.

Through the implementation of MASID, barangay officials can improve administrative efficiency, strengthen accountability, and enhance transparency in service delivery. Residents, on the other hand, can benefit from easier access to announcements, schedules, and community updates, promoting greater participation and trust in local governance. Ultimately, the proposed system supports the broader goal of digital transformation in local government by providing a modern, reliable, and accessible platform for barangay operations and public service.

The study aims to address the challenges faced by barangays in the management of essential public services, particularly in the areas of payout management, resource distribution and dissemination of community announcements and events. Current manual and inconsistent processes can lead to delays, inefficient recordkeeping, limited transparency and difficulty communicating important information to residents. In view of these problems, this study proposes the development of MASID: An Integrated Barangay E-Services Web Application that aims to streamline these core services through a centralized digital platform.
Specifically, the study sought to answer the following questions:
How can an integrated web application improve the management of barangay payouts by providing accurate beneficiary records, automated scheduling, and real-time monitoring of transactions?
How can the proposed system enhance the efficiency and transparency of resource distribution through centralized inventory management, beneficiary tracking, and distribution monitoring?
How can the web application improve the dissemination of barangay announcements, events, and public information to ensure residents receive timely, accurate, and accessible updates?

How can a Priority Scheduling Algorithm be formulated and implemented to sequence beneficiary payout batches and resource allocation based on validated demographic and vulnerability criteria (such as Senior Citizens, PWDs, Solo Parents, and Indigent residents)?

What is the level of software quality and user acceptability of the MASID system as evaluated by barangay officials, staff, and residents based on the ISO/IEC 25010 software quality standards in terms of functional suitability, usability, reliability, performance efficiency, and security?

This study aims to develop MASID: An Integrated Barangay E-Services Web Application to improve the delivery of barangay services by streamlining payout management, resource distribution, and the dissemination of community events and announcements. The proposed system seeks to enhance operational efficiency, promote transparency, and provide residents with a more accessible and reliable platform for accessing barangay services and information.
Develop a web-based payout management module that enables accurate beneficiary record management, automated scheduling, and real-time monitoring of payout transactions.
Design and implement a resource distribution module that facilitates centralized inventory management, beneficiary tracking, and efficient monitoring of resource allocation and distribution.

Create an events and announcements dissemination module that provides residents with timely, accurate, and accessible information regarding barangay activities, public services, and community announcements.

Formulate and implement a Priority Scheduling Algorithm that dynamically sequences beneficiary payout schedules and claims according to weighted priority criteria (e.g., Senior Citizens, PWDs, Solo Parents, and Indigents).

Evaluate the developed system using the ISO/IEC 25010 software quality model to determine its functional suitability, performance efficiency, usability, reliability, security, and overall acceptability among its intended users.

This study presents the design, development, and implementation of MASID: An Integrated Barangay E-Services Web Application. It is a web-based system that intends to deliver a central digital platform to streamline some of the barangay services. The system is built on three main pillars of functionality: managing payouts, distributing resources, and broadcasting community events and announcements. The application provides modules for managing beneficiary information, scheduling and tracking of payouts, maintaining resource inventories, recording assistance distribution, publishing announcements and event schedules, and generating reports to support administrative decision making. It also offers secured user authentication and role-based access for barangay administrators and authorized personnel. It allows residents to access public announcements, event information, and other pertinent barangay updates through the web application. The study also encompasses the testing and evaluation of the proposed system to assess its functionality, usability, reliability, performance, security, and overall acceptability among its intended users. The results of the evaluation will determine the effectiveness of the system in improving the efficiency, transparency, and accessibility of barangay service delivery.

The proposed system is designed to manage payout records, resource distribution, and the dissemination of community events and announcements through a web-based platform. Several limitations are acknowledged:
The system is designed for implementation within a single barangay and is not intended for multi-barangay or municipality-wide deployment.
The application is web-based and requires an internet connection for users to access its features and services.
The system is limited to three primary functions: payout management, resource distribution, and the dissemination of barangay announcements and events.
The application does not support online financial transactions, electronic fund transfers, or integration with banking and digital payment platforms.
The system does not integrate with external government databases or information systems for automatic verification of resident or beneficiary records.
The application is intended for use by authorized barangay personnel and registered residents, with access controlled through user authentication and role-based permissions.
The evaluation of the proposed system is limited to assessing its functionality, usability, reliability, performance, security, and user acceptability during the testing phase.

The study is significant as it aims to provide a digital solution to the challenges encountered by barangays in managing and delivering essential services to the community. Through the development of MASID: An Integrated Barangay E-Services Web Application, the study seeks to improve the efficiency of barangay operations by streamlining payout management, enhancing resource distribution processes, and providing a more effective platform for disseminating community events and announcements. The proposed system may help improve record accuracy, promote transparency, and provide residents with easier access to important barangay information and services.
The findings and implementation of this study are expected to benefit the following stakeholders:

The study provides barangay officials with a centralized platform for managing payout records, monitoring resource distribution, and disseminating community announcements. It helps reduce manual processes, improve record accuracy, and support more efficient decision-making in delivering public services.

The system assists barangay staff by simplifying administrative tasks such as managing beneficiary information, tracking distributed resources, organizing event information, and generating reports. This can help improve productivity and reduce errors caused by manual record-keeping.

The proposed application benefits residents by providing easier access to important barangay information, including payout schedules, available resources, and upcoming events. It promotes better communication between residents and barangay authorities by ensuring that relevant updates are accessible through a digital platform.

This study may serve as a reference for future researchers and developers who intend to create or improve digital solutions for local government services. It can provide insights into the application of web-based systems in enhancing barangay operations and community engagement.

REVIEW OF RELATED LITERATURE AND STUDY

The advancement of information technology has significantly transformed the way organizations manage services, records, and communication. In local government settings, digital systems have become increasingly important in improving the efficiency, transparency, and accessibility of public services. Barangays, as the primary units of local governance, handle various community services such as financial assistance distribution, resource management, and information dissemination. However, traditional manual processes may result in challenges such as inefficient record-keeping, delays in service delivery, and difficulties in maintaining accurate and accessible information. This Review of Related Literature presents studies and technologies that discuss the use of web-based information systems for digital government services, barangay management platforms, resource distribution systems, and information dissemination technologies.
2.1.1 Defining digital transformation: Results from expert interviews

studied digital transformation in government organizations and emphasized how digital platforms improve public service delivery, accessibility, and communication between government institutions and citizens. The study highlighted that adopting digital systems allows organizations to replace inefficient manual processes with automated and centralized platforms that support better information management and citizen engagement.
2.1.2 Management Information Systems: Managing the Digital Firm

explained that management information systems help organizations collect, process, store, and distribute information to improve operational efficiency and decision-making. Information systems provide centralized data management, reduce errors caused by manual processes, and allow organizations to access accurate information when needed.
2.1.3 United Nations E-Government Survey 2022: The Future of Digital Government.

discussed the importance of e-government development in improving public service delivery through digital technologies. The report emphasized that online government platforms increase accessibility, improve communication, and allow citizens to receive services and information more efficiently.
2.1.4 Priority Scheduling Models in Public Resource Allocation and Municipal Services

Algorithmic scheduling models, particularly Priority Queuing and Fair Queuing algorithms, have been increasingly investigated in public administration and disaster management systems to optimize resource distribution and citizen service. When public subsidies or relief resources are released, conventional first-come, first-served methods frequently result in overcrowding, extended wait times, and health risks for vulnerable populations such as elderly citizens and persons with disabilities. Research on municipal service scheduling emphasizes that incorporating weighted priority classification into distribution platforms allows local authorities to dynamically organize beneficiaries into orderly time windows based on vulnerability metrics, thereby maximizing throughput, eliminating bottleneck delays, and ensuring equitable access to vital assistance.
2.1.5 Multi-Criteria Decision Making and Filtering in Community Welfare Delivery

Data filtering and multi-criteria classification algorithms serve as a critical foundation for modern community e-governance applications. Studies in local government informatics indicate that manual resident sorting and paper-based verification frequently produce record discrepancies, duplicate aid disbursement, and delayed reporting. Implementing multi-criteria filtering algorithms allows local administration systems to instantaneously query and segment demographic records across multiple parameters, such as income level, family structure, disability status, and historical assistance claims. This algorithmic segregation enhances administrative transparency, simplifies regulatory auditing, and provides decision-makers with real-time analytics regarding community welfare needs.
2.1.7 BALANGAY: A web-based document request and incident reporting system with decision support for barangay program development.

E-Government systems have brought significant changes on the way public services are easily being delivered nowadays. This motivates the researchers to contribute to this innovation by developing a system named “BALANGAY” which makes barangay services more accessible to the constituents. This is anchored with the objectives of the study which is mainly to build a centralized database for barangays and design modules with the purpose of streamlining barangay processes. Part of it is to generate an incident heatmap that will assist barangay officials in creating better programs and project developments. The study is a combination of qualitative and quantitative type of research which is reflected on the use of interview and survey questionnaires. An iterative waterfall methodology was also adopted as a guide in the development process. Meanwhile, the ISO 9126 Software Quality Model was used in the system evaluation wherein each response is measured using the 5-point Likert scale and respondents were selected using purposive sampling. The result shows that out of sixteen (16) barangay constituents and sixteen (16) IT experts who participated, most of them were very satisfied with the system with a weighted mean of 4.45 and a verbal interpretation of “Very Satisfied”.

International literature highlighted the importance of e-government and information systems for improvement of efficiency, transparency and accessibility, and local researches emphasized the effectiveness of web-based solutions for barangay operation. This study is anchored on the concept of digital transformation in public service, which emphasizes the use of information and communication technology to improve the accessibility, efficiency, transparency, and delivery of government services. The framework is primarily guided by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), which explains that users are more likely to adopt and utilize a technological system when they perceive it as useful and easy to use. In the context of Masid, the system is designed to provide barangay residents and officials with a convenient platform for accessing essential services, particularly in managing payouts, distributing resources, and disseminating information about barangay events. The framework also incorporates the principles of E-Governance, which promote the use of digital technologies to enhance communication, service delivery, accountability, and citizen participation in local government. Through the integration of these principles, Masid aims to reduce manual processes, minimize delays and errors, improve the organization and monitoring of beneficiaries and resources, and provide timely information to residents. The system further supports the concept of Information Systems Success, wherein the quality of the system, information, and services influences user satisfaction and overall effectiveness. By providing accurate information, organized records, accessible services, and timely announcements, Masid is expected to improve the overall efficiency of barangay operations and enhance the experience of residents in receiving public services. Therefore, the theoretical framework assumes that the integration of digital technology into barangay services, supported by usability, perceived usefulness, information quality, and effective service delivery, can contribute to more efficient, transparent, and responsive barangay governance.

The developmental research design will be used in the design and development of Masid, an integrated web-based barangay e-services application intended to streamline payout management, resource distribution, and the dissemination of barangay events and announcements. This design is appropriate because the study involves the systematic identification of user requirements, planning of system functions, designing of the application, implementation of the proposed system, testing, and refinement.

The developmental process will begin with the identification of the existing procedures used by the barangay in managing beneficiaries, payouts, resources, announcements, and events. Information gathered from barangay personnel and residents will be translated into functional and non-functional system requirements. These requirements will serve as the basis for designing and developing the Masid web application.

The descriptive-evaluative research design will be used to describe the existing processes and evaluate the developed system based on the perceptions and experiences of its intended users. The evaluation will focus on the system's functionality, usability, reliability, performance efficiency, security, and overall acceptability.

Through the combination of developmental and descriptive-evaluative approaches, the researchers will be able to develop a system based on actual user requirements and determine whether the resulting application satisfies the intended operational needs of the barangay.

The study adopted the Agile Software Development Model in the development of Masid: An Integrated Barangay E-Services Web Application. Agile is an iterative and incremental approach that allows the development team to plan, develop, test, evaluate, and improve the system through repeated development cycles. The model was selected because it provides flexibility in responding to changing requirements and allows improvements to be included throughout the development process. Agile was chosen because the system consists of three major functional areas: the payout management, resources management and the event management of barangay announcements. Each functional area can be developed and tested allowing the development team to know what are the errors and make improvements before proceeding to development activities.
Figure 3.1. Agile Software Development Model Adopted by the Study

Requirements gathering is the initial stage of the system development process. In this stage, the development team identifies and understands the needs, concerns, and expectations of the intended users. The main purpose of this stage is to determine what the system should provide and what problems it should help solve. Gathering accurate requirements is important because these requirements will serve as the foundation for the design and development of the system.

In the development of the proposed system, the development team gathers information from barangay officials, staff, and residents to identify the functions that are needed in the system. The team considers how different barangay activities are currently handled, particularly in managing beneficiaries, scheduling payouts, distributing resources, monitoring available supplies, and communicating announcements and community events. The team may also identify difficulties experienced by users, such as manual record-keeping, delays in updating information, or difficulty in monitoring distributions. The information collected during this stage will be used as a basis for determining the features and functions that MASID should include.

After the necessary requirements have been identified, they are organized into a product backlog. A product backlog is a structured list of the features, functions, improvements, and tasks that need to be completed during the development of the system. It provides the development team with a clear overview of what needs to be developed and helps the team determine which requirements should receive greater attention.

The identified requirements are then translated into features such as beneficiary management, payout scheduling, resource inventory, distribution monitoring, announcements, and event management. Each feature can be arranged according to its importance, urgency, and usefulness to the intended users.functions related to managing beneficiaries and payouts may be given higher priority because these are essential to the main operations of the system. Prioritizing the backlog allows the development team to focus on the most important requirements first while ensuring that other features can be addressed in succeeding development cycles.

Sprint planning is the stage where the development team decides which tasks and requirements from the product backlog will be developed during a specific sprint. Since the entire system cannot be developed and completed at the same time, the team divides the work into smaller and more manageable parts. During this stage, the team identifies the tasks that can realistically be completed within the given sprint period.

During the development process, the team may select a specific module or set of related functions as the focus of a sprint. For instance, the team may initially work on the payout management module, including the recording of beneficiaries, scheduling of payouts, and monitoring of payout status. The team discusses the tasks that need to be completed, determines the expected output, and assigns responsibilities among the members. Proper sprint planning helps the team maintain a clear direction and ensures that the selected tasks are achievable within the planned development period.

The sprint, also referred to as an iteration, is the stage where the selected requirements are transformed into actual system features. During this period, the development team performs activities such as designing, coding, testing, integrating, and improving the selected functions. A sprint is conducted within a limited period, allowing the team to work on a specific set of requirements instead of attempting to complete the entire system at once.

At this stage, the team begins developing, by creating and developing a particular feature, such as the beneficiary management or payout management. Once the feature is developed, it is tested to determine whether it performs according to the identified requirements. If errors or problems are found, the team makes the necessary corrections and improvements. The completed feature may then be integrated with other parts of the system. This process is repeated through several sprints until the major functions required for MASID have been developed and properly integrated.

After a sprint is completed, the developed features are reviewed by the development team and, when applicable, presented to the intended users or stakeholders. This stage allows the team to determine whether the developed functions meet the actual needs of the users. Feedback is important because the development team may not identify all usability concerns or missing requirements during the development process alone.

The developed features are then presented to barangay officials, staff, and other intended users to evaluate the developed features based on their usefulness, accuracy, and ease of use. For users may provide feedback regarding the payout management feature if some information is difficult to locate or if an additional function is needed. The team can use this feedback to identify errors, clarify requirements, and determine possible improvements. The concerns and suggestions gathered during the review can then be added to the product backlog and considered in the next sprint. In this way, the system continuously improves based on the actual experiences and needs of its users.

Deployment is the stage in which the developed and sufficiently tested system or system increment is made available for actual use. Before deployment, the development team ensures that the necessary features have undergone testing and that identified problems have been addressed. The team may also verify that the system functions properly in the intended environment and that authorized users can access the appropriate features.

Once the system is ready for implementation, it is made available to authorized barangay personnel and, depending on the system's intended functions, residents who are allowed to use or access specific services. Once deployed, the system can be used to support activities such as beneficiary management, payout monitoring, resource distribution, announcements, and event management. However, deployment does not necessarily mean that development completely ends. The system can continue to be monitored after implementation, and additional improvements may be made based on user feedback, newly identified issues, changing requirements, and future needs of the barangay. This allows MASID to remain useful, functional, and responsive to the users it is designed to serve.

The study was conducted within the jurisdiction of Barangay 442, Zone 44, District IV, located in the Sampaloc district of the City of Manila, Philippines. Barangay 442 is a vibrant urban community situated in close proximity to major thoroughfares and educational institutions in Manila's University Belt. The barangay is home to a diverse population of permanent residents, senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PWDs), solo parents, and low-income families who rely on local government assistance programs, periodic cash payouts, and disaster relief goods. The Barangay Hall serves as the primary administrative and frontline service center where officials and staff manage resident registrations, financial aid dispersals, and community announcements. Prior to the implementation of MASID, Barangay 442 handled these vital operations using paper blotters, manual logbooks, physical bulletin boards, and mobile megaphone announcements. These manual practices led to severe administrative bottlenecks, crowding during payout events, duplicate assistance claims, and communication gaps between the barangay council and constituents, establishing Barangay 442 as an ideal locale for the design, deployment, and empirical evaluation of the MASID integrated e-services platform.

The respondents of the study comprised individuals directly involved in the administrative operations and public service utilization of Barangay 442, Sampaloc, Manila. A total sample size of forty-five (N = 45) respondents participated in the evaluation of the system, categorized into three distinct stakeholder groups:

1. Barangay Officials (n = 5): Comprising the Barangay Captain, Barangay Secretary, Barangay Treasurer, and Kagawad Committee Chairpersons. Selected through Purposive Sampling based on their executive authority and direct responsibility for approving budgets, overseeing payout programs, and governing public policy. 2. Barangay Staff and Distribution Personnel (n = 10): Comprising administrative assistants, inventory keepers, and field disbursement officers. Selected through Purposive Sampling due to their hands-on operational role in encoding beneficiary data, managing relief inventory, verifying recipient identities, and operating the system modules. 3. Barangay Residents and Beneficiaries (n = 30): Comprising registered residents belonging to priority categories (Senior Citizens, PWDs, Solo Parents, and 4Ps/indigents). Selected through Convenience and Stratified Random Sampling to evaluate user experience, ease of navigating announcements and schedules, and overall system accessibility from a citizen perspective.

The data-gathering procedure will be conducted systematically to obtain the information needed for the analysis, design, development, and evaluation of the proposed
Masid: An Integrated Barangay E-Services Web Application for Streamlining Payouts, Resource Distribution, and Events Dissemination Using Priority Scheduling Algorithms and Filtering Algorithms.

This procedure aims to collect relevant and reliable data that will serve as the foundation for the design, development, and evaluation of the proposed web application. The researchers will gather information regarding the existing processes involved in barangay payouts, resource distribution, and events dissemination, as well as the challenges encountered by both barangay personnel and residents in accessing and managing these services.

The researchers will first prepare the instruments needed to obtain accurate information regarding the existing barangay processes, particularly those involving payouts, distribution of resources, announcements, events, beneficiary identification, prioritization, and record management.

The first instrument will be a structured interview guide to be used with key personnel of the barangay such as the Barangay Captain, Barangay Secretary, Treasurer, personnel who have been tasked to handle payouts or assistance, and other staff who are directly involved in the distribution of resources and dissemination of community-events. The interview questions will focus on the present workflow, issues faced, the amount of time required for processing, how beneficiaries are identified, how requests are prioritized, how records are maintained, how announcements are made and the information that personnel require from an integrated system.

The second instrument will be a questionnaire to ascertain the perceptions and needs of potential users. The questionnaire might consist of the respondent profile, current barangay processes, problems experienced in gaining access to services or information, desired features of the system, perceived benefits of automation, and assessment of the proposed Masid system. Likert-scale statements can be used to describe functionality, usability, efficiency, reliability, security, and user satisfaction.

The third instrument is a checklist for document review. This will be used in recording pertinent information from barangay documents and records. These can be payout lists, beneficiary records, distribution records, event schedules, announcements, forms, reports, and other documents that represent the current processes. The checklist will help the researchers identify the data fields, approval procedures, categories, eligibility indicators and other requirements that need to be represented in Masid.

The instruments will be reviewed by the research adviser and qualified validators before actual data collection. Necessary revisions will be made to improve the clarity, relevance, completeness, and appropriateness of the questions. Particular attention will be given to privacy because barangay systems may process personal and household information. DILG guidance emphasizes that information collected from inhabitants should be accompanied by appropriate privacy information and that organizational, physical, and technical safeguards should be implemented when personal information is processed.

After the instruments have been prepared and approved, the researchers will coordinate with the barangay officials to schedule interviews. The interviews will be conducted with selected personnel who have direct knowledge of the processes that Masid intends to digitize.

Before each interview, the researchers will explain the purpose of the study, the expected duration, the use of the information, and the confidentiality of the respondents' answers. Permission will be requested before recording or taking detailed notes.

The interview will cover the current payout and resource allocation workflow. Researchers will study existing processes for identifying beneficiaries, receiving and evaluating requests, prioritizing, allocating available resources and documenting completed transactions. Other questions will address how barangay officials disseminate information on events, programs, payouts and the availability of resources.

Special attention will be paid to the identification of conditions transformable into priority rules. For example, the barangay may prioritize based on urgency, kind of assistance, category of beneficiary, deadline, or other criteria. The researchers will also record the actual rules employed by the barangay and not assume that every transaction should be automatically accorded the same priority.

The interviews will also identify problems associated with manual procedures, such as duplicate records, difficulty locating documents, delayed processing, inconsistent prioritization, difficulty monitoring distributions, and limited reach of announcements. These findings will serve as requirements for the design of Masid.

After the interviews, questionnaires will be distributed to the identified respondents based on the approved sampling procedure of the study. The respondents may include barangay officials, barangay staff, and selected residents or beneficiaries who are expected to interact with the system.

The researchers will explain the instructions for answering the questionnaire and clarify that respondents should provide answers based on their actual experiences with barangay services. Sufficient time will be provided for completion. For respondents who have difficulty answering digital questionnaires, printed questionnaires may be provided when appropriate.

After completion, the questionnaires will be retrieved and checked for completeness. Questionnaires with missing responses will be reviewed according to the study's established rules for handling incomplete data. The collected responses will then be encoded into a dataset for statistical analysis.

The questionnaire will provide quantitative evidence that can complement the qualitative information obtained through interviews. This combination is useful in system-development research because interviews can explain the reasons behind existing problems, while questionnaires can measure the extent to which those problems or requirements are experienced by a larger group of respondents.
3.5.4 Review of Relevant Documents and Records

The researchers will conduct a documentary review to understand the existing barangay procedures and the actual information used in transactions. With appropriate authorization, relevant documents may include beneficiary lists, payout records, resource-distribution records, event calendars, announcement materials, transaction forms, reports, and other records related to the scope of Masid.

The researchers will not reproduce unnecessary personal information in the research documentation. Instead, records will be examined primarily to identify system requirements, workflow rules, and data structures. This is particularly important because DILG's Barangay Information Management System initiative emphasizes centralized and organized management of barangay information while also stressing data privacy and security.

The documentary review will also allow the researchers to compare what respondents report during interviews with what is reflected in actual records. This comparison will help identify inconsistencies and prevent the system requirements from being based solely on individual perceptions.
After completing the interviews, questionnaires, and documentary review, the researchers will organize all collected information according to the objectives of the study.

The data collected through interviews, questionnaires, observations and relevant documents and records will be organized, reviewed and analyzed to determine common concerns, existing practices, user needs and system requirements. The researchers will compare the information collected from different sources to find common findings and to find discrepancies that may need to be explained further. Both qualitative and quantitative data will be used to develop a broader understanding of the current barangay processes in terms of payouts, resource distribution, events dissemination, and information management.

The result of the analysis will then be validated to the respondents, barangay personnel and other knowledgeable persons to ensure that the identified requirements really represent the actual needs and processes of the barangay. The validated results will be used to identify the features, functions, workflows, prioritization criteria, filtering requirements and other specifications that need to be incorporated into Masid.
3.5.6 System Development and Preparation for Testing
Once the requirements have been validated, the researchers will translate the findings into the functional and non-functional requirements of Masid.
The proposed system will include functions relevant to the identified barangay processes, such as:

The priority scheduling algorithm will be designed based on the validated criteria identified during requirements analysis. Instead of processing all requests in an identical sequence, the system can assign a priority value according to approved barangay rules. Requests with higher priority can then be placed ahead of lower-priority requests when the applicable conditions require it.

Priority-based approaches have been studied in information systems for managing requests and improving the processing of higher-priority activities. Research on priority scheduling for web portals, for example, found that classifying requests according to priority can improve the processing performance of higher-priority requests. Dynamic priority scheduling has likewise been investigated in data-dissemination systems where requests have different timing requirements.

For Masid, the priority mechanism should therefore be based on the barangay's actual policies and requirements. The researchers will document the criteria, assign appropriate priority levels, and ensure that the resulting queue is transparent and understandable to authorized personnel.

The filtering algorithm will be implemented to allow authorized users to efficiently locate relevant records. Filters may include beneficiary category, transaction type, date, status, priority level, event category, distribution type, and other fields identified during requirements gathering.

The system will then undergo preparation for testing. Test accounts, sample records, test scenarios, and expected results will be prepared. Testing data will preferably use dummy or controlled information rather than unnecessary real personal information.

The development process will follow an appropriate software-development methodology. Recent Philippine research on barangay information systems has demonstrated the use of iterative development approaches such as Scrum, while other studies have applied SDLC phases including planning, analysis, design, implementation, and maintenance.
3.5.7 Scheduling and Conduct of System Testing

After preparing the initial release of Masid, the researchers will work with the target users and testers to develop a proper timetable for testing the system. Testing will utilize produced scenarios and demo activities to establish whether the system is working in accordance with its specifications. Researchers will analyze the overall operation of the system, which includes aspects such as functionality, usability, system efficiency, dependability, security, and responsiveness performance.

The users will experiment with the application during user-testing, carrying out certain tasks that are typical for the barangays. All the errors, discrepancies, problems, and unexpected outcomes will be recorded, evaluated and analyzed by the researchers. The data will provide information for the improvement of the system before it is finalized.
3.5.8 Collection and Analysis of Evaluation Results

Once the system testing phase is complete, evaluation instruments will be passed on to the respondents and evaluators selected to evaluate Masid. The evaluation will enable the respondents to share their views regarding how well the system was able to perform various functions in terms of effectiveness, reliability, usability, accessibility, security, and efficiency in the provision of barangay services. The respondents may also provide feedback in the form of their observations, comments, and suggestions based on their experiences with the system.

The evaluation results obtained shall go through the processes of organizing, tabulating, and analyzing them through the proper statistical approach. The results will be interpreted to find out if Masid is generally accepted and effective, as well as to point out the strengths and areas for improvement. The researchers will utilize the results, along with the suggestions and remarks generated by the evaluators, to finalize the necessary improvements to the created system.

The DFD Level 0, also known as the Context Diagram, provides a high-level representation of the MASID system as a single process. It illustrates the interaction between the three primary external entities - the Administrator, Barangay Staff, and Resident - and the Integrated Barangay E-Services System.

The diagram shows the inputs provided by each user type, such as login credentials, beneficiary data, payout program details, resource inventory entries, announcements, and event information, and the outputs generated by the system, including dashboard analytics, payout transaction records, distribution reports, public announcements, event schedules, notifications, and audit logs.

The Administrator provides system configuration, user management commands, and full operational data, and receives comprehensive reports, audit trails, and system-wide analytics. The Barangay Staff provides beneficiary registrations, payout processing, resource inventory updates, and distribution records, and receives operational dashboards, schedule information, and transaction confirmations. The Resident provides login credentials and profile information, and receives payout schedules, announcements, event information, and personal notifications through the public-facing portal and resident dashboard.

The System Architecture Diagram presents the overall structure of the proposed MASID: Integrated Barangay E-Services System. It shows how the different user types interact with the system through the Presentation Layer, how the Business Logic / Application Layer processes requests and executes system operations, and how the Database Layer stores and manages all system data. This diagram provides a high-level view of how the different components work together to support integrated barangay e-services management.

The system employs a three-tier architecture. The Presentation Layer is built using React with TypeScript and Vite as the build tool, providing a responsive single-page application (SPA) interface with role-based views for administrators, staff, and residents. The Business Logic / Application Layer handles all serverside processing through a RESTful API, implementing JWT-based authentication, role-based access control (RBAC), and modular service logic for each functional domain. The Database Layer uses MySQL (masid_db) with the utf8mb4 character set and unicode collation to store and manage all persistent data across 13 relational tables with defined foreign key constraints and indexing strategies for optimal query performance.

The specified Hardware Requirements are designed to provide the necessary computing, storage, connectivity, and power resources for the effective operation of the system. Since Masid is a web-based application, the main hardware components include a server or hosting computer, desktop or laptop computers for barangay personnel, smartphones or tablets for residents, network devices, backup storage, and power protection equipment. The server will handle the application, database, user accounts, transactions, records, reports, and processing of the priority scheduling and filtering functions, while administrator computers will be used for managing payouts, resource distributions, beneficiaries, events, announcements, and other barangay services. Residents may access the system using smartphones, tablets, or other internet-enabled devices through a web browser. For reliable operation, the server should have at least a Core i3/Ryzen 3 processor, 4 GB RAM, and 256 GB SSD, while the recommended configuration is a Core i5/Ryzen 5 processor, 8–16 GB RAM, and 512 GB SSD. Administrator computers should have at least 4 GB RAM and an SSD, while 8 GB RAM or higher is recommended for smoother multitasking.

In addition to computing devices, Masid will require reliable network and supporting hardware to maintain continuous access and protect important information. A router and, when necessary, a network switch will provide connectivity among the barangay office devices and the internet, while backup storage such as an external HDD, SSD, or NAS will be used to maintain copies of the system database and important records. A UPS will provide protection against sudden power interruptions and help prevent data loss or hardware damage. Printers and scanners may also be provided to support remaining paper-based activities, such as printing reports, transaction documents, or digitizing relevant records. The hardware requirements should also consider future expansion, including an increasing number of residents, beneficiaries, transactions, stored records, and simultaneous users. Overall, the selected hardware should provide sufficient performance, reliability, storage capacity, and connectivity to support the daily operation of Masid while allowing the system to be expanded as the barangay's digital service requirements grow.

Software testing will be conducted to determine whether the proposed MASID: Integrated Barangay E-Services System functions according to its specified requirements.

The testing process will assess the correctness of the system’s individual functions, the interaction among its integrated components, and its acceptability to the intended users. It will also verify whether the system properly manages beneficiary records, processes payout transactions, maintains accurate resource inventory, publishes announcements and events, and enforces role-based access control across all user types.

The proposed system will undergo three levels of testing: Unit Testing, Integration Testing, and User Acceptance Testing. Each testing level will employ an appropriate testing approach. White-box testing will be applied during Unit Testing, gray-box testing will be employed during Integration Testing, and blackbox testing will be used during User Acceptance Testing. Test cases will be prepared to specify the function to be tested, the input data or action to be performed, the expected result, the actual result, and the corresponding status of each test.
3.8.1 Unit Testing Using the White-Box Approach

Unit Testing will be conducted by the researchers using the white-box testing approach. This approach will allow the researchers to examine the internal logic, conditions, calculations, and processing paths of the individual system components. Since the researchers will have access to the system’s source code, they will be able to determine whether each function and module has been implemented according to the established requirements.

The modules to be tested will include user authentication and authorization, resident profile management, beneficiary registration and management, payout program creation and configuration, payout schedule management, payout transaction processing, resource inventory management, resource distribution recording, announcement creation and publishing, event management, notification generation, report generation and export, audit log recording, user account management, and system settings configuration. Each module will be tested independently before it is connected to the other components of the system.

The role-based access control (RBAC) mechanism will also be examined as individual processing components. The authentication module will be tested to determine whether it correctly validates login credentials, generates JWT tokens, and enforces session management. The authorization module will be tested to determine whether it properly restricts access based on user roles (admin, staff, resident) and prevents unauthorized access to protected routes and API endpoints. Predetermined test data will be prepared to evaluate the different conditions involved in each module’s operation. These conditions will include beneficiary category validation, payout amount calculations, resource quantity tracking, stock threshold alerts, announcement publication workflow, and event scheduling logic.

The researchers will test both valid and invalid conditions to ensure that the system follows the required processing paths. Cases involving incomplete information, duplicate records, invalid data formats, boundary values (e.g., zero quantity, negative amounts), and unauthorized access attempts will also be included.

For every test case, the researchers will compare the actual output with the expected output. A test will be marked as passed when the actual result corresponds with the expected result. When an error or unexpected result is identified, the affected function will be reviewed and corrected. The component will then be tested again to verify that the correction has resolved the defect without negatively affecting its other functions.
3.8.2 Integration Testing Using the Gray-Box Approach

Integration Testing will be conducted after the individual modules have successfully undergone Unit Testing. The researchers will use the gray-box testing approach because they will possess knowledge of the system’s architecture, database structure, modules, and data-processing procedures while evaluating the system through its interfaces and outputs. This testing stage will determine whether the React.js frontend, the RESTful API backend, MySQL database, role-based access control, and reporting functions communicate and function correctly as an integrated system.

The researchers will examine whether data entered through the user interface are properly transmitted to the backend, validated based on the defined system rules, stored in the appropriate database tables, retrieved accurately, and displayed correctly to the user. The testing will cover the interaction among the authentication, resident management, beneficiary management, payout program, payout schedule, payout transaction, resource inventory, resource distribution, announcement, event, notification, report generation, and audit logging modules.

For example, when a new beneficiary is registered, the researchers will verify whether the beneficiary record is properly linked to the corresponding resident, whether the beneficiary code is generated correctly, and whether the registration is reflected in the beneficiary management dashboard. When a payout transaction is processed, the researchers will verify whether the transaction amount is correctly recorded, the beneficiary’s claim status is updated, the resource inventory is adjusted (if applicable), the notification is generated, and the audit log entry is created. Complete transactions will be performed to evaluate the flow of information throughout the system.

These transactions will begin with the entry or modification of data and will continue through database storage, API processing, notification generation, and presentation of the final results. The generated reports will be reviewed to determine whether beneficiary, payout, resource, distribution, and event information remain accurate and consistent across the interconnected modules. The interaction between the frontend and backend API endpoints will also be tested. The researchers will determine whether the API correctly handles authentication tokens, enforces role-based permissions, validates input data, returns appropriate error messages, and maintains data consistency during concurrent operations.

The results will be examined for data integrity issues, permission violations, missing notifications, incomplete audit logs, and inconsistent report outputs. When an integration issue is encountered, the researchers will trace the affected data flow and determine whether the error originated from the frontend, backend, database, API communication, or inter-module logic. The identified issue will be corrected, and the complete transaction will be performed again until the expected result is achieved.
3.8.3 User Acceptance Testing Using the Black-Box Approach

User Acceptance Testing will be conducted after the completion of Unit Testing and Integration Testing to assess whether the completed MASID: Integrated Barangay E-Services System meets the requirements and expectations of its intended users.

The evaluators will assess the system based on its functions, inputs, outputs, and observable behavior without examining its source code or internal implementation. Selected barangay personnel who are knowledgeable about beneficiary management, payout distribution, resource inventory, community event coordination, and announcement dissemination will participate as system evaluators.

Their participation will help determine whether the completed system satisfies the operational requirements of Barangay 442, Sampaloc, Manila and whether it is suitable for its intended purpose. Before the testing begins, the researchers will provide the participants with a brief orientation regarding the objectives, features, and basic operation of the proposed system. The evaluators will then be provided with representative tasks that reflect the actual barangay e-services management process. These tasks will include accessing the system, logging in with different user roles, adding and updating resident profiles, registering and managing beneficiaries, creating payout programs, scheduling payouts, processing payout transactions, managing resource inventory, recording resource distributions, creating and publishing announcements, managing events, viewing the dashboard, generating reports, and reviewing notifications and audit logs. The evaluators will enter the required data and observe the corresponding output of the system. The actual results will be compared with the expected results indicated in the prepared acceptance test cases.

The tests will determine whether the system properly validates user inputs, saves and retrieves records, enforces role-based access, processes payout transactions, tracks resource inventory, publishes announcements, manages events, generates notifications, and presents accurate information. After completing the assigned tasks, the evaluators will assess the proposed system using a structured User Acceptance Testing questionnaire. The evaluation will cover relevant system-quality characteristics such as functional suitability, usability, reliability, performance efficiency, and overall user satisfaction. The evaluators will also be allowed to provide comments, identify difficulties encountered, and recommend possible improvements.

The completed questionnaires will be collected, tabulated, and analyzed using the statistical treatment established for the study. The findings will be used to determine whether the proposed system meets the requirements and expectations of its intended users. Any relevant technical issue or recommendation identified during the evaluation will serve as a basis for further system revision and improvement.
3.8.4 Documentation and Evaluation of Test Results

The results of Unit Testing, Integration Testing, and User Acceptance Testing will be documented using structured test-case forms. Each test case will contain the test-case identifier, testing objective, input data or action, expected result, actual result, and test status. A test case will receive a status of Passed when the actual result corresponds with the expected result. It will receive a status of Failed when the system produces an incorrect, incomplete, or unexpected result. All failed test cases will be recorded and reviewed by the researchers.

The identified defects will be classified according to the affected module or system component. Necessary corrections will then be applied, followed by retesting to determine whether the issue has been resolved. Previously tested functions related to the corrected component will also be examined again when necessary to ensure that the modification has not introduced additional errors. The system will be considered ready for final implementation when its essential modules operate correctly, its integrated components exchange and process information consistently, and its intended users determine that it is acceptable for barangay e-services management activities.

The combined use of white-box, gray-box, and black-box testing will provide a comprehensive assessment of the proposed system. White-box testing will verify the internal logic of the individual components, including authentication, beneficiary management, payout processing, and resource tracking modules. Black-box testing will validate the system’s overall functionality and usability from the perspective of the barangay administrators, staff, and residents who will operate it in a real-world environment.

The conduct of this research strictly complied with the ethical guidelines for academic research and the legal mandates of Republic Act No. 10173, also known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012. Prior to participation, all barangay officials, personnel, and resident respondents were fully informed regarding the objectives, scope, and evaluation procedures of the study, and their voluntary written informed consent was secured. No respondent was subjected to coercion or risk, and participants were explicitly informed of their right to withdraw from the evaluation at any time without prejudice. To guarantee strict confidentiality, personal identifiers such as resident full names, home addresses, contact numbers, and financial assistance amounts were anonymized and processed solely in aggregate form for academic analysis. Furthermore, the test datasets and database credentials utilized during testing were isolated within a secured local environment, ensuring that no sensitive constituent information was exposed or shared externally.

The MASID E-Services system follows a simple and organized navigation flow designed to help residents easily access barangay information and services. For users who need personalized services, the Sign In page provides account access, while new users can select Create Account to register. After that, the user starts at the Home page, where they can view the main navigation options, explore available services, check announcements, view upcoming events, and access payout schedules. From the Services section, users can choose services such as Payout Assistance, Resource Assistance, Events, Announcements, Request Information, and Contact Barangay. The Payouts page provides residents with schedules, locations, requirements, and important reminders for different assistance programs. The Events page displays upcoming barangay activities with their dates, times, locations, and descriptions, while the Announcements page provides the latest community updates and important notices. Users can also access the About the Masid page to learn about the system, its purpose, features, and Barangay 442 information. The Contact Barangay page allows users to view contact details and send a message through an online form. Overall, the navigation flow connects the Home page to the major system sections—Services, Payouts, Events, Announcements, About Masid, Contact Barangay, and Account Access—allowing residents to move easily between public information and online barangay services.

The Masid E-Services System consists of the information and actions provided by residents and barangay personnel through the platform. This includes account information such as email addresses, passwords, and registration details, as well as information submitted through the Contact Barangay form, including the user’s name, email address, phone number, subject, and message. Users also provide input by selecting different services, viewing payout schedules, checking announcements, exploring upcoming events, and accessing other available barangay information. In return, the system is the organized information and services presented to users based on their requests and inputs. These outputs include payout schedules, assistance program requirements, community events, barangay announcements, available e-services, contact information, and system information about Masid. Submitted inquiries and requests are also recorded and made available for barangay personnel to manage and respond to. Overall, the system transforms user inputs into accessible, organized, and updated barangay information and services, helping improve communication, transparency, and accessibility for the residents of Barangay 442.

The Masid E-Services System are focused on providing a clean, organized, and user-friendly experience for residents of Barangay 442. The interface uses a consistent color scheme of blue, teal, and white, which gives the system a professional and government-service-oriented appearance. Information is arranged into clear sections and cards, making important services such as payouts, announcements, events, and barangay assistance easy to find. The navigation bar provides quick access to the Home page, Services, Payouts, Events, Announcements, About Masid, and Contact Barangay, while the Sign In button is clearly visible for users who need to access their accounts. The system also uses recognizable icons, readable text, buttons, labels, and spacing to help users understand the available options without confusion. Its responsive layout allows the pages to adjust to smaller mobile screens, as shown in the screenshots, making the system accessible through smartphones as well as larger devices. Overall, the design emphasizes simplicity, accessibility, consistency, and ease of navigation so that residents can quickly locate information and use the available barangay services.
